 '-I'+str(base/'source/include'),'-I'+str(base/'source/lib/qdldl/include'),
 'cpp/cuda/tests/qoco_transpose_benchmark.cu','-L'+str(base/'final'),'-lqoco','-o',str(binary)],check=True)

test_fixture_correction.explanation: The original unit test inspected the private d_csc_host pointer of unused empty CPU-reference transposes. Without the KKT oracle those are legitimately unmaterialized. UBSan localized the null access to the test comparison. The test now requests the physical representation via the accessor; the separately named access_test binary passes with/without the KKT oracle and all four CUDA sanitizer tools. Frozen original binaries and failure evidence are retained. The host ASan attempt failed during CUDA allocation and is not a validation pass.

reproduction.provenance_correction: The earlier manifest omitted the three transpose helper headers. All three are now included and independently compared against the untouched frozen v75 source. This changes provenance only, not the prepared runtime source.

sanitizer_scope: Twenty-five transpose/lifetime cases and nine numerical-update cases pass all four tools. Full landing memory/leak and N500 memory/init/sync run without materializing debug oracles. Forced reconstruction after caller index-array/stream destruction passes normally and under all four tools, both with and without the KKT oracle. Native, landing, N20 and N500 numerical oracles pass.
ownership_scope: Eight eager, eight host-lazy, eight device-deferred fixtures and one deferred chain. Cases verify exact stable ordering, inverse maps, duplicates, empty matrices, signed zeros, no initial host/device arrays or gather, retained source after source/sibling destruction, safe chained destruction and lazy CPU access. Numerical updates invalidate materialized device/host caches, refresh exact values and reuse topology.
